project.name: gopherstack
project.description: Gopherstack is a lightweight, in-memory AWS cloud stack that emulates 150+ AWS service APIs in a single Go binary, with real cross-service integrations (event source mappings, SNS to SQS fan-out, Lambda execution) and a built-in web dashboard.

nodes.name: cli.go

layers.name: Service Emulators
layers.description: Per-AWS-service backends and HTTP handlers under services/<svc>/: wire structs, routing, in-memory backend with a coarse RWMutex, error mapping and persistence snapshots, plus embedded data JSON (e.g. IAM managed policies, CloudFormation attributes).

layers.name: Shared Packages
layers.description: Reusable libraries in pkgs/ (awserr, awstime, safemap, lockmetrics, persistence, httpclient, logger, tags, page, worker, telemetry, etc.) and internal/ helpers used across services; also the shared service-registration plumbing.

layers.name: Entry Point and Cross-Service Wiring
layers.description: main.go and the Kong-based cli*.go files: server bootstrap, Echo router assembly, service registration, lifecycle, and the cross-service adapters (Lambda/S3/ECS/EventBridge targets, CloudControl handlers, IMDS, DNS) that connect emulators.

layers.name: API Contracts and Dashboard Backend
layers.description: Protobuf/Connect RPC definitions in proto/ and the dashboard/ Go package that serves the admin API and embeds the SvelteKit UI.

layers.name: Dashboard Frontend
layers.description: SvelteKit + Vite + Tailwind web console in ui/: routes, components, stores, API clients and Vitest/Playwright config.

layers.name: Developer Tooling and Audits
layers.description: cmd/* analysis and codegen tools (parity lint, route collision checks, enum/error-code audits, gendocs, PGO load), scripts/, bench/, and demo/modules helpers.

layers.name: Integration and E2E Tests
layers.description: test/ suites that drive the built binary via the AWS SDK and cross-SDK e2e smoke scripts, plus their internal helpers.

layers.name: Terraform Fixtures and Examples
layers.description: Terraform resource fixtures under test/terraform that validate AWS compatibility against the emulator, and runnable examples/.

layers.name: Documentation
layers.description: README, CHANGELOG, SECURITY, docs/ architecture and service pages, and per-service PARITY.md parity reports.

layers.name: Build, Packaging and CI
layers.description: Dockerfiles, compose files, Taskfile, goreleaser, golangci/codecov/renovate configs, go.mod, PGO profile and GitHub Actions workflows.

layers.name: AI Agent Configuration
layers.description: Instruction and rule files for coding agents (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, .agent/.cursor/.gemini/.codex/.windsurf/.clinerules, .mcp.json) and analysis output.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: The README introduces Gopherstack as a single Go binary that emulates 150+ AWS service APIs in memory, with real cross-service behavior and a built-in dashboard. Read it first to learn the goals before diving into the code.

tour.title: Process Entry Point
tour.description: main.go is the thin binary entry point that hands control to the CLI layer. cli.go then builds configuration, constructs the service providers and starts the HTTP servers, making it the best place to see the whole runtime assembled.
tour.languageLesson: Go binaries start at func main in package main; heavy lifting usually lives in ordinary package files that main calls.

tour.title: Core Routing and Registry
tour.description: The pkgs/service package defines the Service interface, the registry that holds every emulated service, and the router that dispatches an incoming AWS request to the right one. These abstractions are the contract every service in services/ implements, so they are required reading before any individual emulator.
tour.languageLesson: Go interfaces are satisfied implicitly: each service just implements the methods, with no explicit implements declaration.

tour.title: Shared Helper Packages
tour.description: Small reusable packages carry repo-wide conventions: lockmetrics wraps the coarse per-backend RWMutex, persistence provides snapshot save and restore, awserr holds shared AWS error types and page gives generic pagination. CLAUDE.md states the rule that services reuse these helpers instead of reimplementing them.

tour.title: S3 Emulator
tour.description: The S3 service shows the standard per-service layout: provider.go registers the service, handler.go parses and routes REST requests, buckets.go and store.go hold the backend state, and persistence.go snapshots it. Its PARITY.md records how closely the emulation tracks real S3.

tour.title: DynamoDB Emulator
tour.description: DynamoDB follows the same provider, handler, store and persistence pattern but adds a JSON/CBOR wire layer, an expression engine and item and table operations. Reading it after S3 shows how a different protocol style fits the same service skeleton.

tour.title: Cross-Service Integrations
tour.description: Real behavior across services is wired in the root cli_*.go files and in per-service cross-service hooks. DynamoDB streams feed Kinesis, S3 events reach Lambda, and adapters in cli_adapters.go bridge one service's backend to another without a direct import.
tour.languageLesson: Small consumer-side interfaces plus adapters let packages stay decoupled while still integrating.

tour.title: Lifecycle and Background Behavior
tour.description: cli_lifecycle.go and related runtime files model realistic delays and state transitions, and CloudFormation resource handlers drive other service backends from template properties. Together they show how the emulator goes beyond static CRUD responses.

tour.title: Dashboard Backend
tour.description: The dashboard package serves the embedded web UI and exposes a Connect RPC API whose contract is defined in a protobuf schema. It reads the same service backends as the AWS APIs, so the UI shows live emulator state.

tour.title: Dashboard Frontend
tour.description: The ui directory is a SvelteKit and Vite app that is built into dashboard/static and embedded in the binary. Its connect-client talks to the backend from the previous step.
tour.languageLesson: Svelte 5 runes (.svelte.ts files) provide reactive state outside components.

tour.title: Testing and Test Harnesses
tour.description: Test helpers such as sdktest, teststack and awstest start real service stacks so tests can drive them with the genuine AWS SDK. The cross-SDK end-to-end suite then checks wire compatibility from other languages.
tour.languageLesson: Go tests live beside the code in _test.go files and use t.Parallel with table-driven subtests.

tour.title: Build, Packaging and CI
tour.description: Taskfile.yml defines the build and test targets, the Dockerfile and compose files package the server, and the GitHub Actions ci.yml pipeline runs lint, unit, integration and Terraform tests.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows are YAML files of jobs and steps triggered by events such as push and pull_request.

tour.title: Documentation and Architecture Notes
tour.description: The docs directory holds architecture deep dives and per-service guides, while CHANGELOG.md records releases. These explain design decisions such as DNS, Lambda execution and chaos injection that the code alone does not make obvious.
